metaDescription: PSB Vt 3 tugi is a lesser yam variety. About 8 days to harvest, 12.7 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: PSB Vt 3 is a registered tugi variety. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1993. It takes about 8 days from planting to harvest, with 12.72 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about PSB Vt 3 tugi
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

PSB Vt 3 tugi takes about 8 days from planting to harvest. That is 8.8 days faster than the average of the 3 lesser yam varieties with a day count, 17.3 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 12.72 t/ha beats the average of its group, 12. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.
Dry matter is 34.88 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne. The starch content is 16.76 percent.
Where and when to plant PSB Vt 3 tugi
It is recommended for anywhere in the country. Tugi is a hardy yam for backyards and uplands. Pick by tuber size and taste.
